Event.description: Event is what only an event has, on the actor it is.

address.description: Where it is held, when it is somewhere. Sent to the same people as the address to join online, and for the same reason: it may be somebody's home. HasAddress says there is one all the same.

has_address.description: Whether it has an address, said to everybody.

viewer_rsvp.description: What the viewer has answered: going, maybe, or left out.

site_name.description: The site it is on, as it calls itself.

administration.description: Whether the viewer may look after it: on a profile, its settings.

post.description:
Nobody is told: the person reported never learns of the report or who made it, and administrators find it in their queue. A thing the viewer cannot see answers exactly as one that does not exist, so that reporting is no way to find out what is hidden. Twenty reports an hour at most.

Who may call it: somebody signed in, with a token that carries `account:write`.

details.description: What the reporter adds in their own words. Needed where the reason says so.

target_id.description: The id of what is reported: a post, a reply, a profile.

200.description: the viewer had reported it already; their report was updated

400.description: not well formed; or `own_content`, it is the viewer's own; `reason_not_applicable`, the reason is not for this kind of thing; `details_required`, the reason needs the reporter's own words

401.description: no token, or one that has expired

403.description: the viewer may not do this

404.description: there is no such thing that the viewer can see

429.description: too many reports in the last hour
